report.source_text: In the days following her operation, the patient was admitted to the ICU, where she faced pancreatic fistula that resolved with non-operative care. Her glucagon and glucose blood levels dropped dramatically post-operatively (Table 1). One week after the surgery, the patient's cutaneous lesions almost disappeared.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 44-year-old woman presented with a 3-month history of pruritic rash involving extremities and oral cavity progressing to groin, abdomen, axillae, and gluteal region. Admission labs revealed hyperglycemia and diabetes mellitus diagnosis, with elevated chromogranin A and serum glucagon. Physical exam showed well-demarcated erythematous plaques with fragile vesicles. Abdominal imaging identified a 3-cm enhancing pancreatic head mass. Histopathology of the biopsy confirmed pancreatic neuroendocrine carcinoma with vascular and perineural invasion. Post-operative course included ICU admission for pancreatic fistula, which resolved with non-operative care. After surgery, glucagon and glucose levels dropped, and the skin lesions resolved almost completely within one week.
